instruction: Use the peg to poke the cube into the goal region.

outcome.real_measurement: Rationale: the task's own goal: cube CENTRE within the 5 cm goal disc at every judged step (user ruling 2026-11-14: centre, not footprint; E13 P22 accomplished). Real world: top camera, cube centroid vs the printed target, 1 s after the robot stops.
Rationale: at rest: cube speed <= 2 cm/s at every judged step (as v2). Real world: frame differencing.

Rationale: stays put: the cube moves <= 2 mm from where it was at the window's first step (closes E13 P21: a creep under the 2 cm/s bound moved it 6-9 mm inside a 1 s window). Real world: tracked centroid, 1 s.
Rationale: lying on the table (|centre height - half size| <= 5 mm; a cube on the 5 cm peg is 50 mm up; unchanged from v2). Real world: RGB-D / side camera.

Rationale: the peg touched the cube: >= 1 control step with peg-cube impulse accumulated over all substeps >= 5e-4 N*s (unchanged from v2). Real world: camera track of the peg head touching the cube face while it moves, or F/T along the peg.

Rationale: tool use = the robot's own links do not move the cube. Counted: the cube's net in-plane displacement from the start of each robot-cube contact episode (any robot link, any physics substep) until the cube is at rest (<= 5 mm/s) or the peg touches it (so a flick that only accelerates the cube, then lets it coast, is counted), summed over episodes. Bound 5 mm (user ruling 2026-11-14: E10 P4 s0, a hand brush that moved the cube ~3 mm followed by a peg poke, is accomplished; the E1 gripper push moves it ~10 cm; a vertical load that does not move the cube, E13 P24, counts ~0). Replaces v2's total-impulse rule: PhysX contact impulses are normal-only, so an impulse bound both over-counts vertical loads and misses friction drags (E15 probe: a fingertip dragged the cube 24.7 mm with 0.04 N*s in-plane impulse). Real world: cube displacement (camera) during and after any hand-cube contact (tactile / F/T with the peg load subtracted, or proximity < 5 mm).

notes: Protocol v3 (veritask/adapters/protocol_v3.py). After the policy's last action the evaluator HOLDS the robot where it stopped (hold A: every arm switched to a pd_joint_pos hold of the joint positions reached at the policy's last step, drive-velocity targets zeroed, grippers keep their last commanded opening; any control mode). It steps until the scene is quiescent for settle.quiet_steps = 10 consecutive control steps (0.5 s: every quiet_max signal under its bound at every step, every quiet_disp group moved <= its bound, largest arm-joint speed <= 0.01 rad/s, measured from joint POSITIONS over each control step: PhysX's reported joint velocity stays at 0.012-0.043 while nothing moves when the robot presses through a held object or closes its fingers on one, E15 development runs; finger joints excluded) and then judges the following 1.0 s window (20 steps); if no quiescence leaves room for the window inside settle.max_seconds = 3.0 s the episode is rejected. End-state terms (trace.window_*) read only the judged window; event terms (trace.count_true / trace.max) read the episode up to the window's end. Hold B (switch, not the default): the evaluator replays the policy's last action and robot joint speed must stay <= settle.robot_speed_max at every window step. Constants: max_seconds 3.0 = room for the slowest legitimate transient seen (a fast-pushed cube at rest 0.3 s after the last action, E13 P23; a held robot settles in < 0.5 s, E15 probe) with margin; quiet_steps 10 = 0.5 s of stillness; robot_speed_max 0.01 rad/s (about 5-8 mm/s at the TCP; a held robot reaches 1e-4 rad/s within 0.5 s, E15 probe; E13's creeping policies ran at 0.04-0.09 rad/s).  Holding the peg at the end is allowed (require_released false). Quiescence for this task: cube and peg each <= 2 cm/s and moved <= 1 mm over the 10 quiet steps, robot joint speed <= 0.01. Not checked: that the cube's final motion was caused by the peg rather than by a third object (none exists in the scene).
